ucs.title: [LLM] OilRig (APT34) PowerShell backdoor DNS-tunneling C2 (BONDUPDATER / QUADAGENT / Helminth)
ucs.description: Hunts the DNS-over-PowerShell command-and-control channel that defines APT34's custom backdoor family — a scripting engine emitting a high volume of distinct, high-entropy subdomain lookups under a single registrable domain (TXT/A beaconing). This is OilRig's signature C2, not generic DNS noise.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.message_type=Query AND DNS.query!="" by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.record_type _time span=1h
| rex field=DNS.query "(?<subdomain>.*)\.(?<reg_domain>[^.]+\.[^.]+)$"
| stats dc(DNS.query) as unique_subdomains sum(count) as total_queries values(DNS.record_type) as record_types min(_time) as firstTime by DNS.src reg_domain
| where unique_subdomains > 100 AND total_queries > 200
| eval note="High distinct-subdomain fan-out under one parent domain = DNS-tunnel C2 (APT34 BONDUPDATER/QUADAGENT pattern)"
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| sort - unique_subdomains
ucs.kql:
// Defender lacks a raw DNS-query table; pivot on scripting engines making DNS (port 53) traffic — anomalous for PowerShell
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where RemotePort == 53
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize DnsLookups = count(), DistinctResolvers = dcount(RemoteIP), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where DnsLookups > 50      // 50 = scripting-engine DNS volume is near-zero in baseline; tunneling beacons exceed this fast
| order by DnsLookups desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where isnotempty(Name)
| where QueryType in ("TXT","A","AAAA","CNAME","NULL")
| extend labels = split(Name, ".")
| where array_length(labels) >= 3
| extend reg_domain = strcat(tostring(labels[array_length(labels)-2]), ".", tostring(labels[array_length(labels)-1]))
| summarize UniqueSubdomains = dcount(Name), TotalQueries = count(), RecordTypes = make_set(QueryType), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated)
    by ClientIP, Computer, reg_domain
| where UniqueSubdomains > 100 and TotalQueries > 200   // tunnel fan-out: many unique labels under one parent
| order by UniqueSubdomains desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationPort:53 @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\CScript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.EXE)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?<reg_domain>[^.]+\.[^.]+)$", field=DomainName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, reg_domain], function=[count(field=DomainName, distinct=true, as=unique_subdomains), count(as=total)])
| unique_subdomains > 100
ucs.rationale: APT34 (OilRig / Helix Kitten / Hazel Sandstorm / Evasive Serpens) is distinguished from most state actors by its near-exclusive reliance on DNS-tunnel C2 across its bespoke PowerShell backdoors — Helminth, ISMAgent, BONDUPDATER, QUADAGENT — which encode beacon data into high-entropy subdomain labels and TXT responses. ucs.title: [LLM] OilRig (APT34) Outlook Home Page persistence / code-exec registry implant (T1137.004)
ucs.description: Detects modification of the Outlook WebView/Today 'home page' registry URL — APT34's favored mail-client persistence and re-execution mechanism that loads attacker-controlled HTML to relaunch its backdoor when Outlook opens. Distinctively OilRig given their heavy Exchange/webmail-centric tradecraft.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\Outlook\\WebView\\*\\URL" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\Outlook\\Today\\UserDefinedUrl" OR Registry.registry_value_name="URL" Registry.registry_path="*\\Outlook\\WebView\\*") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_id _time
| where match(Registry.registry_value_data, "(?i)^https?://")
| rename Registry.* as *
| table _time dest user registry_path registry_value_name registry_value_data process_id
| sort - _time
ucs.kql:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has "\\Outlook\\" and (RegistryKey has "WebView" or RegistryKey has "Today")
| where RegistryValueName in~ ("URL","UserDefinedUrl")
| where RegistryValueData matches regex @"(?i)^https?://"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("RegistryValueSet","SetValue","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has "\\Outlook\\" and (RegistryKey has "WebView" or RegistryKey has "Today")
| where RegistryValue in~ ("URL","UserDefinedUrl")
| where RegistryValueData matches regex @"(?i)^https?://"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT34 Outlook Home Page Persistence Registry Set
id: 6e2a1c4f-2b7d-4f3a-9c1e-0a7f2d3b8e10
status: experimental
description: Detects setting of the Outlook WebView/Today home-page URL registry value, an APT34 (OilRig) persistence and re-execution technique.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1137/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0049/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1137.004
  - attack.t1112
logsource:
  category: registry_set
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_key:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\Outlook\WebView\'
      - '\Outlook\Today\'
    TargetObject|endswith:
      - '\URL'
      - '\UserDefinedUrl'
  selection_value:
    Details|startswith:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
  condition: selection_key and selection_value
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate enterprise Outlook home-page GPO customizations (rare; baseline first)
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\Outlook\WebView\*\URL OR *\Outlook\WebView\*\url OR *\Outlook\Today\UserDefinedUrl OR *\Outlook\Today\userdefinedurl) @Details:(http\://* OR https\://* OR HTTP\://* OR HTTPS\://*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegObjectName=/\\Outlook\\(WebView|Today)\\/i
| RegValueName=/(URL|UserDefinedUrl)$/i
| RegStringValue=/^https?:\/\//i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ucs.rationale: The Outlook Home Page implant (T1137.004) is a low-prevalence technique strongly associated with Iranian mail-centric operators, and APT34 (OilRig / Cobalt Gypsy / Evasive Serpens) repeatedly leverages Exchange/Outlook-resident persistence and webmail-based tradecraft.
